  Pays a pending payment order by debiting a customer account. It checks the account type, confirms the order exists and is pending, works out the commission from the company or general service tariff, and verifies available funds. It then debits the account through sp_debito, adds a separate commission debit when required, and marks the order paid in pg_orden. Any failure rolls back, sets an error code and message, and ends through sp_cerror; success returns 'PAGO REALIZADO'.

response.content: {"observations": ["sp_pago_orden is the only unit and the only entry point: 173 lines, 10 blocks, 20 decisions. The migration is one unit, so the work is about splitting it cleanly, not about untangling dependencies between units.", "Blocks B6-B8 form the transaction phase: the account debit, the optional commission debit and the update of pg_orden. They must commit or roll back together, so define the transaction boundary first.", "The debit goes through the external proc db_cuentas..sp_debito, which is not in the inputs. Its behavior, its own transaction handling and its error codes must be documented, or the migrated flow could double-debit or leave partial debits.", "Error exit B10 rolls back, sets an error code and message, and ends through cobis..sp_cerror, another external unit that is not provided. The error contract that callers see depends on it and needs to be replicated or mapped.", "All four tables have unknown schemas and are known only through this code. Concurrent payments of the same order are a risk unless the read and the update are protected, so check locking and isolation.", "Business rules RF-01 to RF-08 are well delimited in blocks B1-B8, which makes them good candidates for rule-by-rule extraction and testing. B6 and B9 have no rule label and need review to see what they do.", "Commission logic is spread over B3 (company tariff, else general), B4 (web pays half, payroll pays none) and B7 (separate movement).
